### Sternoclavicular (SC) joint
- **Only true joint** linking the upper limb to the axial skeleton; saddle type, **intra-articular disc**

### Acromioclavicular (AC) joint
[[FIG: Fig 2.13 · 2.04
- **Horizontal** stability → **AC ligaments** · **vertical** stability → **CC ligaments**
  - **Conoid** → **posteromedial**, vertical, ≈**4.5 cm** from the lateral end → the more important vertical stabiliser

- Like the pelvis → one break in a ring → look for the second

### The joint
[[FIG: Fig 2.15 · 2.05
- **Static** GH (glenohumeral) stabilisers → glenoid + **labrum**, capsule and **GHLs** (glenohumeral ligaments), negative pressure · **dynamic** → **rotator cuff**, long head of biceps
- **Labrum** → deepens the glenoid ≈**50%**, ≈**20%** of stability · blood from capsule and periosteum, **not** bone · **anterosuperior** poorest

[[FIG: Fig 2.16 · 2.05

### Glenohumeral ligaments
| Ligament | Tight in → stops |
|---|---|
| **SGHL** (superior) | **Adduction** → inferior translation + ER |
| **MGHL** (middle) | **45° abduction** → anterior translation |
| **IGHL** (inferior) — anterior band | **90° abduction + ER** → anterior–inferior dislocation → **the most important** |
| IGHL — posterior band | **Flexion + IR** (internal rotation) → posterior translation |
| **CHL** | Adduction → inferior translation (with SGHL) |

- Between the two IGHL bands → **axillary pouch** → contracted in frozen shoulder

### The four cuff muscles
[[FIG: Fig 2.23, 2.24 · 2.06
| Muscle | Insertion | Nerve | Action |
|---|---|---|---|

### Force couples, cable & biceps pulley
[[FIG: Fig 2.25, 2.26 · 2.06
| Couple | Limb 1 | Limb 2 |
|---|---|---|
| **Vertical (coronal)** | Deltoid pulls the head **up** | Cuff pulls it **down and in** |
| **Horizontal (axial)** | Subscapularis (front) | Infraspinatus + teres minor (back) |

- Couple lost → head rides up → **acromiohumeral distance** falls → cuff arthropathy · complete imbalance → **pseudoparalysis**
- **Biceps pulley** = **CHL + SGHL + supraspinatus + subscapularis** · upper subscapularis tear → long head subluxes **medially**

### Coracoacromial arch
- **Acromion + CA ligament + coracoid** → roof over the supraspinatus and the subacromial bursa
  [[FIG: Fig 2.27, 2.28 · 2.06

- **Acromial branch of the thoracoacromial artery** runs with the CA ligament → bleeds in subacromial decompression
- CA ligament → last restraint to **upward migration** in a cuff-deficient shoulder → do not cut it there

### Impingement — five types & the numbers
- "Which impingement syndromes?" → **five**

2.09.b:
### Axillary artery
- **Outer border of the 1st rib** → **lower border of teres major** · **pectoralis minor** divides it → **part 1 → 1 branch, part 2 → 2, part 3 → 3**
  [[FIG: Fig 2.35 · 2.09

| Part | Branches |
|---|---|
| 1st (above pec minor) | **Superior thoracic** |
| 2nd (behind pec minor) | **Thoracoacromial**, **lateral thoracic** |
| 3rd (below pec minor) | **Subscapular** (→ circumflex scapular + thoracodorsal), **anterior** and **posterior circumflex humeral** |

- Rule → "**Screw The Lawyer, Save A Patient**"

### Blood supply of the humeral head
- **ACHA** (anterior circumflex humeral artery) → **ascending branch** in the groove → **arcuate artery** (Laing) → classic "main supply"
  [[FIG: Fig 2.36 · 2.09
- **PCHA** → newer work: **64%** of the head's blood → **both matter**
- **Hertel** criteria (head viable) → **metaphyseal extension ≥8 mm** + **intact medial hinge** → fix; otherwise → replace

PITFALL — which circumflex feeds the head?
- Classic → **ACHA** (arcuate artery of Laing) · Hettrich 2010 → **PCHA ≈64%** → many 4-part fractures do not get AVN (avascular necrosis)
- Say both: "ACHA by tradition, PCHA by newer perfusion studies"

### Anastomosis around the scapula
- Links the **1st part of the subclavian** artery with the **3rd part of the axillary** artery
  [[FIG: Fig 2.37 · 2.09

| From | Artery | Course |
|---|---|---|
| **Subclavian** (thyrocervical trunk) | **Suprascapular** | Over the transverse scapular ligament → supraspinous fossa → round the **spinoglenoid notch** → infraspinous fossa |
| **Subclavian** (or deep branch of the transverse cervical) | **Dorsal scapular** | Down the **medial border**, deep to the rhomboids |
| **Axillary** (3rd part) → subscapular | **Circumflex scapular** | Through the **triangular space** → infraspinous fossa |
| Small contributors | **Posterior intercostals**, **acromial** branches | Medial border; round the acromion |

MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "anastomosis around the scapula" (Prof Shamaa)
- Joins the **subclavian (1st part)** to the **axillary (3rd part)**
- From the subclavian → **suprascapular** (thyrocervical trunk) + **dorsal scapular** (or deep branch of the transverse cervical)
- From the axillary → **subscapular** → **circumflex scapular** (through the triangular space) + thoracodorsal
- Extra → posterior **intercostals**, acromial branches → meet in the infraspinous fossa, along the medial border and round the acromion
- Use → ligation of the axillary artery **proximal to the subscapular** is safe; collateral in subclavian block and coarctation

HIGH YIELD — what is at risk, by region
- Posterior / lateral portals, deltoid split → **axillary nerve** ≈5 cm below the acromion

| Test | Position → why (anatomy) | Structure | Anatomical trap |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Jobe (empty can) / full can** | Scapular plane; thumb down (empty) or up (full) → **supraspinatus** works alone over the top of the head | Supraspinatus | Empty can is also the impingement position → still weak in **full can** = true weakness (Prof. Maged Samy) |
| **ER lag / hornblower's** | Resisted ER at the side → **infraspinatus**; in **abduction** → **teres minor** | Infraspinatus, teres minor | Suprascapular nerve palsy gives the same |
| **Lift-off / belly press / bear hug** | Hand behind the back / on the belly (**elbow in front of the trunk** so pectoralis major cannot help) / on the other shoulder → only **subscapularis** pushes IR | Subscapularis | Increased passive ER also suggests the tear (Prof. Maged Samy) |
| **Neer / Hawkins** | Flexion / flexion + IR → brings the **greater tuberosity under the CA arch** | Supraspinatus + bursa | Positive in many shoulders → not specific |
| **Apprehension / relocation** | 90° abduction + ER → loads the **anterior IGHL band** and anteroinferior labrum | IGHL, Bankart | Pain only (not apprehension) → posterior/internal impingement |
(Netter)
[[FIG: Fig 2.46 · 2.14

- **Passive ER in adduction** → CHL / rotator interval → limited = true stiffness (frozen, arthritis); near-normal = cuff tear (Prof. Maged Samy)
- **Sulcus** (pull the adducted arm down) → SGHL + CHL + interval → not lost when ER is added = interval lesion
- **O'Brien** (90° flexion, 10° adduction, thumb down) → biceps anchor (SLAP) · pain on top → AC joint instead
- **Speed / Yergason** (resisted flexion / supination) → long head in its groove · **cross-body adduction** → AC joint · **wall push** → winging (→ Scapulothoracic)
